findings.statement: TNFa pathway activity is higher at baseline in ustekinumab non-responders (BH padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000484]) and also in UNIFI placebo non-responders (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.00608]), but not in PURSUIT placebo (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (PURSUIT).padj=0.932]); it marks severity rather than a drug-specific mechanism.

NFkB activity shows the same pattern as TNFa: higher in non-responders to ustekinumab, golimumab, infliximab, vedolizumab and corticosteroids (PROTECT), and also in UNIFI placebo non-responders, so it is a shared severity axis; it is not elevated in mesalamine or etrolizumab non-responders.

JAK-STAT activity is higher in ustekinumab non-responders (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0124]) but not in vedolizumab non-responders (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.vedolizumab.padj=0.571]); UNIFI placebo is borderline, so specificity is unproven.

TGFb activity is higher in ustekinumab non-responders (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.000493]) and in UNIFI placebo non-responders, but not in golimumab non-responders (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.golimumab.padj=0.348]); it is a severity-linked rather than anti-TNF-specific signal.

OSM is higher at baseline in ustekinumab non-responders (BH padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000264]) but the drug-vs-placebo interaction does not survive (padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; interaction.ustekinumab.padj=0.982]); the placebo arm trends the same way (padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.116]), so OSM is associated with severity, not a ustekinumab-specific mechanism. The anti-TNF atlas shows no significant cell-state difference.

CXCR2 ranks first in convergence (meta-analysis padj [gene=CXCR2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; padj=4.26e-11]) with clinical-stage antagonists. Higher baseline expression is associated with ustekinumab non-response (padj [gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=9.69e-6]) but also with UNIFI placebo non-response (padj [gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0126]) and not golimumab (padj [gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.golimumab.padj=0.994]); this is a neutrophil/severity marker, not drug-specific.

CXCL8 is higher at baseline in ustekinumab non-responders and in UNIFI placebo non-responders, with no drug-vs-placebo interaction surviving correction. In the adalimumab atlas, no baseline cell-state difference exists, and after treatment it falls in cycling MNP (padj [gene=CXCL8; type=antitnf_singlecell; source=DATASET:GSE282122; after_vs_before_treatment.1.padj=0.0253]) in a cohort of few patients (leads only).

TREM1 is higher in ustekinumab non-responders (padj [gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000474]) but also in UNIFI placebo non-responders (padj [gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0234]); the interaction is not significant, so it marks severity.

IL11 shows the strongest ustekinumab association among the genes checked (padj [gene=IL11; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=3.68e-8]), but UNIFI placebo non-responders also have higher IL11 (padj [gene=IL11; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0133]) and no interaction survives, so it is a severity marker.

IL23A baseline expression is not associated with ustekinumab response (padj [gene=IL23A; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.977]); target abundance does not stratify response to its own drug.

ITGB7 is not associated with vedolizumab response (padj [gene=ITGB7; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.vedolizumab.padj=0.995]), nor with response in any other arm; a negative result for a target-expression biomarker.

CHRDL2 leads the discovery screen (first-in-class opportunity, antibody-tractable, consistently up across cohorts) but is only partly composition-independent (retained share [gene=CHRDL2; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.2764]), made mostly by inflammatory fibroblasts; vital-organ RNA is the highest of the lot (nTPM [gene=CHRDL2; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; vital_max_ntpm=42.6]), a safety question. Genetic and functional support is missing.

CPXM1 is a stromal (inflammatory fibroblast) transcript replicated in a second dataset, with a retained share of [gene=CPXM1; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.4136] after composition adjustment and low vital-organ RNA; it has no clinical drug but also no functional or genetic evidence in UC.

LAX1 is mainly plasma/T-cell derived and the lineage call did not replicate in the second dataset; only a minor share survives composition adjustment (retained [gene=LAX1; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.2300]), so the increase largely reflects immune infiltration rather than a tissue change.

XKR9 is the only top-15 candidate called intrinsic (epithelial; retained [gene=XKR9; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; retained=0.7976]) but is up in only [gene=XKR9; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; cohorts_up=4] cohorts and expressed in few cells, so reproducibility is weak.

caveats: Pathway and gene associations are baseline non-responder vs responder comparisons, not predictions; small arms (infliximab, golimumab, PURSUIT placebo) lack power.
Many ustekinumab hits also appear in UNIFI placebo, indicating severity; no drug-vs-placebo interaction survives correction.
Anti-TNF single-cell cohort is small; results are leads.
Discovery candidates are mostly partly composition-dependent, and have no genetic, functional or in-vivo validation.
Convergence ranking top genes (CXCR2, CXCR1, CXCL8, CD274, IDO1) are neutrophil/inflammation-driven, a composition concern.
